Minister of Mines, Colonel Ousmane Abarchi, makes an official visit to the AMZEGUER gold site

Thirteen months after obtaining its two permits, SGCI presented its achievements at the AMZEGUER site to the Minister of Mines: investments of around two billion CFA francs, seven deep boreholes, a camp, an ore processing plant and a power station.

18 November 2026

Société Générale de Commerce et de l'Industrie (SGCI SARLU) had the honour of welcoming the Minister of Mines of the Republic of Niger, Commissaire-Colonel Ousmane Abarchi, to its AMZEGUER gold site in the commune of Tabelot, Agadez region. The Minister was received by the Chief Executive Officer of SGCI, Mr Abdoulaye Massaoud Yalloni, together with the company's teams.

The Minister was accompanied by officials from the central administration of the Ministry of Mines and by several chief executives of mining companies. The visit was also marked by the presence of distinguished guests, including the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Groupe SOS, Mr Assalih Ibrahim Ari, known as “Saley Boss”.

Two billion CFA francs invested in thirteen months

Only thirteen months after obtaining its permits No. 1 and No. 2, SGCI has already invested around two billion CFA francs at the AMZEGUER site. This covers the development of the project, mapping work and the drilling of seven deep boreholes on site, intended to supply water to the ore processing plant.

The company has also built a camp able to accommodate more than 300 employees, both workers and SGCI managers.

A processing plant, from crushing to leaching

The plant comprises the industrial unit for crushing and grinding the ore, together with the unit that processes the ore by leaching.

This part of the operation is closely monitored: SGCI has put strict measures in place to protect its staff and the environment.

A power station and a solar plant

The site has a power station made up of a series of more than eight generator sets, four of which are already installed and four planned as back-up. A solar plant already supplies the camp.

A detailed field visit

During the visit, the ministerial delegation toured the operating perimeter alongside the Chief Executive Officer, who presented the work in progress and the organisation of the site. Bagged ore lots were presented to the Minister and his delegation, and discussions continued in the field with the technical teams.

SGCI's commitment

For SGCI, this visit is a mark of attention from the highest authorities of the sector towards a Nigerien mining company. It strengthens the company's commitments: to operate in compliance with the Mining Code, to ensure the traceability of the gold produced, and to contribute to the development of communities in the Agadez region.

SGCI's management extends its sincere thanks to the Minister of Mines, to his entire delegation and to the distinguished guests who honoured the site with their presence.
